note: The producer capability descriptor, version 1, for THIS producer. The reference's descriptor is carried verbatim as `reference_descriptor`; `descriptor` is what fwg publishes, and every place the two differ is named in `deviations` -- tools/embed/capabilities.py refuses an undocumented difference, and refuses any change to `kernel` or to the coordinate contract beyond the documented prose. WHY THEY DIFFER: the reference's own contract says the supported inventory must track the actual producer (Contracts/capabilities-and-coordinates.md), and a clean rewrite is a different producer -- copying the reference's inventory would claim world_json 2 and generation_algorithm 16, which a consumer would negotiate and then fail to read. tests/test_capabilities.cpp pins each claimed version against the code that owns it. READ BY: fwg::capabilities_document and fwg::require_capabilities (src/capabilities.cpp), and `fwg capabilities`.

coordinates.height_datum: radial elevation above reference sphere, not sea level

globe.handedness: right-handed Cartesian cross product: X cross Y = Z
globe.poles: unit positions are exact [0, +/-1, 0]; tangent orientation retains anchor longitude

city.height: absolute radial elevation; schematic viewer draws this vertically
city.rotation: degrees; positive width rotation runs from east toward north

patch.mesh: Cartesian surface displacement projected onto the anchor east/up/north frame
patch.rows: south to north; columns west to east

tile.rows: north to south; columns west to east
tile.samples: inclusive boundary indices; tile requests themselves cannot cross a seam or pole

unreal_boundary.axis_mapping: Unreal X is source east, Y is source north, Z is source radial up; left-handed Z-up, so copied triangle winding reverses. Implemented by the native core and the FantasyWorldGenerator plugin, not by this producer.
unreal_boundary.origin: caller-chosen tangent anchor (latitude, longitude, origin height); lengths scale by 100 once at that boundary

kernel.storage: host-owned atomic commit; pending snapshots are checkpoints

deviations.implementation: Names this producer. The reference's value is python-reference.
deviations.supported.generation_algorithm: World::generator_version, which this producer stamps 1 on every world (include/fwg/world.hpp). The reference's 16 names its own algorithm.
deviations.supported.world_json: The world document this producer writes is schema fwg.world version 1 (kWorldSchemaVersion, include/fwg/serialize.hpp), not the reference's fantasy-world-generator.world version 2.
deviations.supported.hamlet_plans_json: HamletPlans::version is 3 (include/fwg/city_plan.hpp). The reference advertised 1 while its own hamlet_planner.VERSION was already 3; its descriptor was stale.
deviations.supported.native_kernel: The counter kernel runs natively here (src/counter_kernel.cpp). The reference listed native_kernel as unavailable from the Python producer.
deviations.unsupported: native_kernel removed: the counter kernel runs natively here (see supported.native_kernel).
deviations.coordinates.unreal_boundary.axis_mapping: "this Python producer" reads "this producer". The mapping itself is unchanged and is not implemented here either.
